explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/668: does the number of incongruent n-point planar sets maximising the number of unit distances tend to infinity? The statement says that for every m, eventually in n, there are m n-point sets attaining maxUnitDistances n (u(n), the sSup of unitDistNum over n-point sets), pairwise non-congruent under plane isometries. That is the right way to say 'the count → ∞', and it handles infinite counts. Faithful.
